answer: A bonded stake makes fake agents expensive: each identity must lock a deposit released only after a long vesting period, and the bond is slashed if two identities are proven to share the same operator, keys, or work output. At dawn of each epoch, the network audits a random sample, so an attacker cannot know which clones will be checked. Like pigment mixed into paint, the bond is inseparable from the identity's history, and umber traces of past behaviour follow it, so thousands of cheap copies cost thousands of forfeited deposits, while one honest agent risks almost nothing.
